items.title: Mississauga's New Rental Licensing Bylaw Aims to Curb Renoviction-Driven Evictions
items.summary: According to INsauga, Mississauga's new Rental Repairs and Renovations Licensing Bylaw took effect Tuesday, aiming to stop landlords from using major repair or renovation claims as a pretext to push out tenants, a practice known as renovictions. The outlet reports city council adopted the bylaw in April after developing it with input from tenants, landlords and community groups across Mississauga. INsauga reports the rules work alongside Ontario's Residential Tenancies Act and are meant to make the eviction process clearer and fairer while reducing housing instability. According to the outlet, city officials said the changes are also intended to help protect Mississauga's supply of affordable rental housing. INsauga reports the bylaw comes after renovictions became increasingly common in the city in recent years, prompting municipal politicians to respond.

items.title: Scaled-Down Lorne Park Condo Proposal Heads to Council After Years of Resident Pushback
items.summary: According to INsauga, a scaled-down condominium proposal for 900 Lakeshore Road West in Lorne Park is heading back to city hall after years of neighbourhood opposition. The outlet reports the site sits beside Richard's Memorial Park and is currently home to a single detached house with a pool. INsauga reports the project was first pitched in 2023 as an 11-storey building with 178 units, revised in 2025 to 10 storeys and 188 units, and has now been reduced again to nine storeys with 161 units. According to the outlet, some residents have dubbed the development a cruise ship because of its bulk, and the 900 Lakeshore Committee has raised concerns over wind effects, damage to the site's Carolinian forest, added traffic, parking overflow onto parkland and groundwater management. INsauga reports the latest version goes before Mississauga's Planning and Development Committee on September 8, with a city report noting the developer would also transfer wooded portions of the property to the city.

items.title: Four Comedians Bring Nostalgia-Fuelled Gen X Humour to the Living Arts Centre This October
items.summary: According to Exclaim!, the City of Mississauga and saugaLIVE are bringing a lineup of Gen X comedians to the Living Arts Centre on October 9 for the GenX Takeover Comedy Tour. The outlet reports the night is billed as a mix of laughter, nostalgia and jokes about getting older, aimed squarely at audiences who grew up in the Gen X era. Exclaim! reports the bill features Real Slim Sherri, Kelly Manno, Dadbod Veteran (Jon Willington), Professor Nick Harrison and Justin Rupple. According to the outlet, tickets are already on sale, and fans can upgrade to a VIP package that includes a post-show meet and greet, a photo opportunity, an autographed poster and swag. Exclaim! reports a buffet dinner add-on will also be available before the show at LIVE Restaurant, located steps from the theatre, with organizers recommending reservations even though walk-ins are accepted.

items.title: Mississauga's Outdoor Pools Open to Dogs for One Last Splash Before Closing for the Season
items.summary: According to the City of Mississauga, dog owners are invited to bring their pets to the city's annual Dog Swim on September 12, giving dogs a last chance to splash in outdoor pools before they close for the season. The city reports the free event has run since 2019 and has grown into a popular end-of-summer tradition that draws dogs and owners together for a day of swimming, exercise and socializing. According to the city, the event also supports the Animal Services Special Care for Animals and Resources Fund, known as SCARF, and while attendance is free, donations help pay for medication, specialized veterinary care, foster support and shelter improvements for animals in the city's care. The city says participating dog owners must register online in advance, complete a mandatory waiver and follow all posted pool rules, and every dog must be up to date on its vaccinations. According to the city, people are not permitted in the pool itself but can watch from the pool deck while their pets swim.

items.title: Mississauga Police Shooting That Killed 19-Year-Old Kaleym Davy Prompts Family March and Fundraising Push
items.summary: According to NOW Toronto, the family of 19-year-old Kaleym Davy is organizing a memorial march this coming weekend after he was shot and killed during an interaction with Toronto police on Delfi Road in Mississauga on August 6. The outlet reports Davy's aunt shared details of the march in a social media post, with the family asking anyone who wants to attend to contact organizers directly for the location rather than publicizing it widely. NOW Toronto reports the march comes as Davy's family continues to press for answers about the circumstances of his death and considers pursuing legal action and representation. According to the outlet, the family has also launched a GoFundMe campaign with a public goal of $45,000, while family members say their overall target is $100,000. NOW Toronto reports the funds raised are intended to cover funeral and burial costs along with legal fees, with the campaign describing the family's goal as giving Davy a proper farewell while helping them find answers and pursue justice.

items.title: Mississauga Arrest Caps Months-Long Human Trafficking Investigation Into Barrie Escort Service
items.summary: According to INsauga, a 50-year-old Barrie man was arrested in Mississauga on the weekend following a months-long human trafficking investigation. The outlet reports Barrie police began investigating in June after receiving information that the man was allegedly recruiting women to provide sexual services for an escort service run out of his home. INsauga reports investigators subsequently identified online ads for sexual services linked to the suspect and executed a search warrant at an address in Springwater Township on August 12. According to the outlet, Michael Brocklebank was arrested in Mississauga without incident this past Sunday. INsauga reports Brocklebank now faces multiple charges, including trafficking in persons, material benefit from trafficking in persons, advertising sexual services and failing to comply with a probation order.
